issues.t: Head gasket failure and overheating (Northstar head bolts)
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs or an engine-hot warning appears, coolant keeps disappearing, white smoke comes from the exhaust, or the coolant tank bubbles.
issues.why: On the Northstar V8 the head bolt threads in the aluminum block can pull out, letting the head gaskets leak. Overheating makes it worse, and owners report it most often at 70,000-100,000 miles.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Ask for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas test. A proper fix needs thread inserts in the block, so get a quote from a shop that knows Northstars, and compare it with the value of the car.

issues.t: Engine burns oil
issues.sym: You need to add a quart of oil every 500-1,000 miles, a low oil warning comes on, or there is blue smoke at startup.
issues.why: Northstar engines of this era are known for high oil use from carbon-stuck piston rings. GM issued bulletins on oil consumption and on knocking with oil use for these engines.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and keep a log. Never let it run low. A shop can try a ring cleaning service, but heavy oil use often means internal engine work.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the lower crankcase and oil pan seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, or oil wet on the bottom of the engine.
issues.why: The seal between the engine block halves and the oil pan on the Northstar commonly leaks with age. GM later improved the sealant. RepairPal lists this as the most common DTS problem.
issues.next: Have the leak source confirmed. The proper repair often means lowering the engine cradle, so it is labor-heavy. Small seeps can be watched, but keep the oil topped up.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from the water pump or thermostat housing
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping, a sweet smell, drips under the front of the engine, or a low coolant warning.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover coolant and oil leaks on Northstar engines and a water pump cover that can let the thermostat housing loosen. Owners also report water pump and coolant crossover seal leaks.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the leak found quickly. Running low on coolant can overheat a Northstar and damage the head gaskets.

issues.t: Stumble or stall when coming to a stop
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, idles rough or stalls as you slow down or stop.
issues.why: GM bulletin 150201 covers stalling or stumbling when coming to a stop on these years.
issues.next: Have a shop read codes and check for engine computer updates and idle control problems. Stalling in traffic is a safety risk, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Misfire and stalling when slowing down
issues.sym: The engine misses and may die as the car slows down, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Several 2006 DTS owners report the engine missing and dying while slowing, at around 45,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Have the codes read when the light is on. Ask the shop to look at ignition coils, plugs and idle control, and check for open recalls such as the ignition switch recall.

issues.t: Speedometer drops out and cruise control quits
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the speedometer jumps around or stops, and cruise control stops working.
issues.why: GM bulletin 99-07-30-015 covers this combination, which comes from a bad vehicle speed signal.
issues.next: Have a shop read the codes and check the speed sensor and wiring. Watch your speed carefully until it is fixed.

issues.t: Delayed or harsh shift into reverse
issues.sym: A delay or a hard clunk when you shift from Park or Drive into Reverse, or no engine braking in D3.
issues.why: GM bulletins from 1998 cover delayed or harsh engagement and late downshifts on the 4T80-E automatic.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition. Ask a shop about the bulletins and a fluid service before considering bigger repairs.

issues.t: Transmission axle seal leaking
issues.sym: Red fluid dripping near the front wheels or on the inner side of a tire.
issues.why: The axle seals on the 4T80-E transmission can leak. One owner was quoted a full transmission overhaul at about 40,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and check the fluid level. A seal alone is a much smaller job than an overhaul, so get a second opinion if a shop wants to rebuild the transmission.

issues.t: Front-end clunk or rattle over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk, rattle or metal-on-metal knock from the front of the car over bumps.
issues.why: GM bulletin 99-03-08-005 covers front-end noise on these years. Worn stabilizer links and bushings are common causes.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. Links and bushings are common parts to replace.

issues.t: Rear air-leveling suspension problems
issues.sym: A Service Air Leveling or Service Suspension message, a rear end that sits low, or a compressor that runs a lot.
issues.why: The rear load-leveling system uses an air compressor and air shocks that wear out or leak with age.
issues.next: Have the system checked for air leaks before replacing the compressor, since a leaking shock will kill a new one.

issues.t: A/C compressor runs all the time
issues.sym: The A/C compressor keeps running even when it should cycle off, which can freeze up the system or reduce fuel economy.
issues.why: GM bulletin 01396 covers A/C compressors that run continuously on these cars.
issues.next: Have the A/C system checked and ask about the bulletin.

issues.t: Heating and A/C door actuators fail
issues.sym: A clicking or tapping noise behind the dash, air coming from the wrong vents, or temperature that will not change.
issues.why: Small electric motors that move the air doors inside the heater box wear out. RepairPal lists this as a common DeVille problem.
issues.next: Have a shop find which actuator has failed. Some are easy to reach and some need dash parts removed.

issues.t: Service StabiliTrak message from a steering angle sensor
issues.sym: A Service StabiliTrak or Service Stability System message, sometimes with traction control turning off.
issues.why: The steering wheel position sensor can fail. GM also has bulletins for several StabiliTrak codes on these cars.
issues.next: Have the stability system codes read. Brakes still work normally, but the car will not help you in a skid until it is fixed.

issues.t: Power window drops into the door
issues.sym: A pop or grinding noise and the window falls into the door, or the window stops moving.
issues.why: The window regulators fail on this generation, often one door after another. It is a common DeVille complaint.
issues.next: Tape or cover the opening to keep rain out and have the regulator replaced. Ask whether the motor is still good.

issues.t: Headlights cut out while driving
issues.sym: One or both headlights go out without warning and may come back later, sometimes with a clicking from the front fenders.
issues.why: Many DTS owners report headlights that shut off at night. Bulbs, ballasts and connections in the headlight system are the usual suspects.
issues.next: Do not drive at night with a dead headlight. Have a shop test the bulb, ballast and wiring rather than just swapping bulbs.

issues.t: Side airbag can deploy unexpectedly or not at all (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, a side airbag that goes off while driving, or one that does not deploy in a side crash.
issues.why: Recall 00V-217 replaced the side impact sensor module. Owners also reported parts delays and repairs that did not fix the problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-217 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open. If the airbag light stays on, have the system checked.

issues.t: ABS brake unit can leak inside (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, traction control or stability warnings, or the rear brakes not balancing correctly.
issues.why: The brake hydraulic control unit can leak internally, so the antilock brakes, traction control or stability control may not work as designed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-114 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can fracture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash the driver airbag may not fill fully and parts could strike you.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator could crack at a weld when it deploys.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-222 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open.

issues.t: Steering gear bolt may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, or a clunk from the front when turning.
issues.why: On a small number of cars a steering gear mounting bolt may be missing and a mounting strap may fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-067 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open.

issues.t: Fuel tank pressure sensor can lead to fuel leaks (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or fuel spilling when you fill up, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The fuel tank pressure sensor on 4.6L Cadillacs can fail and damage fuel system parts, so fuel can leak when refueling.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 03V-238 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open. Do not overfill the tank in the meantime.

issues.t: Ignition switch can turn off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after the key is bumped or with a heavy key ring, and the airbags, power steering and power brakes may stop working. Some cars are hard to start.
issues.why: The ignition switch can slip out of the run position. Many DeVille owners report stalling at speed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-355 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open. Until then, keep only the ignition key and fob on the ring.

issues.t: Heated washer fluid module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning or electrical smell, smoke from under the hood, or washers that stop working.
issues.why: The heated washer fluid module can short and overheat, which can start a fire. GM first added a fuse, then disabled and removed the module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 08V-441 and 10V-240 and have them done free. If you smell burning, stop and turn the car off.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid on the ground, a whining pump, harder steering, or a burning smell.
issues.why: The power steering inlet hose connector may be poorly crimped and can leak fluid, which can reduce steering assist or start an engine fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 06V-105 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open.

issues.t: Power steering line can be rubbed through by a cable (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking, a whining pump or heavier steering.
issues.why: A starter or alternator cable can rub against the power steering return line and wear a hole in it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V-553 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open.

issues.t: Tire and loading label missing (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure and load label on the door pillar is missing or wrong.
issues.why: Some 2010 cars left the factory without the correct tire and loading label.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 09V-480 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open. Use the owner's manual for tire pressures until then.
